messages.author: d8f29a4621e38cf3
messages.subject: binary sampler process
parts:
Hi, everyone. I am wondering if I can get the posterior sample of attribute (binary variable) if I set the monitors like below or I need to sample  att_prob and then use rbnorm(1,1, att_prob  ) to have the posterior sample of attribute . Thanks!

monitors=c("gamma","lambda","beta","delta","theta","attribute")

code=nimbleCode({
  for (n in 1:1000) {
    for (i in 1:10) {
      for (k in 1:7) {w[n, i, k] <- pow(attribute[n, k], Q[i, k])}
      logit(prob[n, i]) <- beta[i] + delta[i] * prod(w[n, i, 1:7])
      y[n, i] ~ dbern(prob[n, i])
    }}
  for (n in 1:1000) {
    for (k in 1:7) {
      logit(att_prob[n, k]) <- gamma[k] * theta[n] - lambda[k]
      attribute[n, k] ~ dbern(att_prob[n, k])
    }}
 
  for (n in 1:1000) {theta[n]~ dnorm(0,1)}
  for (i in 1:10) {
    item_parameter[i, 1:2] ~ dmnorm(item_mu[1:2], item_den[1:2, 1:2])
    beta[i] <- item_parameter[i, 1]
    delta[i] <- item_parameter[i, 2]
  }
  for (k in 1:7) {
    lambda[k] ~ dnorm(0, 1)
    gamma[k] ~ T(dnorm(0, 1),0,)
  }
  item_mu[1] ~ dnorm(-0, 1)
  item_mu[2] ~ T(dnorm(0, 1),0,)
  R[1, 1] <- 1
  R[2, 2] <- 1
  R[1, 2] <- 0
  R[2, 1] <- 0
  item_den[1:2, 1:2] ~ dwish(R[1:2, 1:2], 2)
})

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: binary sampler process
parts:
If you configure the MCMC to have the "monitors" you defined, then you will indeed get posterior samplers for the "attribute" variable:

configureMCMC(model, monitors = monitors)

Or you can add monitors using:

MCMCconfigurationObject$setMonitors(monitors)

No, you do not need to sample att_prob and then use rbnorm to generate samples.

Cheers,
Daniel
